statement.p: Oil leaks out of a tanker at a rate of r=f(t) liters per minute, where t is in minutes. If f(t) = A e^{-k t}, write a definite integral expressing the total quantity of oil which leaks out of the tanker in the first hour.
total quantity = \displaystyle \int_{a}^{b} , where a = and b = .
What are the units of this integral?

static.solution: t, consider the interval [t, t+\Delta t]. During this interval, oil is leaking out at an approximately constant rate of f(t) = A e^{-kt} liters/minute. Thus, the amount of oil which has leaked out during this interval can be expressed as \mbox{amount} = \mbox{rate}\times\mbox{time} = f(t) \Delta t = A e^{-kt} \Delta t. and the units of f(t)\,\Delta t are (liters/minute)\timesminutes = liters. The total amount of oil leaked is obtained by adding all these amounts between t=0 and t=60. (An hour is 60 minutes.) The sum of all these infinitesimal amounts is the integral \mbox{total amount} = \int_0^{60} A e^{-kt} dt.
